finding.problem: The request asks for a note on each confirmation, but only `confirm_element` records a reason. `confirm_wording_fix` (agent) and `confirm_all_proposed` (owner, bulk) also move elements to confirmed and take no reason. Elements confirmed those ways have an empty `confirm_reason`. `confirm_all_proposed` also cannot set a per-element reason, because it has no target Element. Later readers still can't tell why those elements were accepted.
finding.where: SKILL.md Actions: confirm_wording_fix and confirm_all_proposed; Element.confirm_reason

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: The request says each confirmation; confirm_wording_fix and confirm_all_proposed also confirm elements without a reason, so the gap is real but not a seeded conflict.

finding.problem: `reason` is now a required param on `confirm_element`, but `confirm_reason` is declared optional on Element. Nothing stops an empty or blank reason, so the stated goal (a note on every confirmation) isn't enforced. No precondition or invariant ties confirmed review to an existing `confirm_reason`.
finding.where: SKILL.md Element.confirm_reason and Invariants; confirm_element params

findings.label: other-real
findings.why: Nothing enforces a non-blank reason or ties confirmed review to a confirm_reason, so the goal of a note on every confirmation is not guaranteed.

finding.problem: The world fixture E2 is already confirmed (review confirmed) but has no `confirm_reason`. That is the state the change was meant to prevent, and E1 is the only example that covers the new field. The fixtures and examples now disagree with the claim that confirmed elements carry a reason.

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: A pre-existing confirmed fixture E2 without a reason is just legacy seed data and not a defect of this change.

finding.problem: `confirm_element` sets `confirm_reason` before the kernel call, and the Effects text does not say what happens if the kernel call fails. The reason could then be stored on an element that never became confirmed. The reason can also be left over from an earlier attempt on elements in the unknown state.

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Speculative about kernel call failure ordering; the spec doesn't establish a real failure and a stale reason is overwritten on the next confirm.

edit.why: It adds a reason on confirm_element stored on the element, but other confirmation paths (confirm_wording_fix, bulk confirm) get no note, so not every confirmation is covered.
